Build three marketing features for the Nxeon platform (Next.js App Router + Prisma + Tailwind) at /opt/nxeon on THIS box. Match existing patterns (read neighbors first). These are customer-acquisition features.

## PART 1 — New free tools (top-of-funnel, shareable, SEO)
Existing free tools live under `app/(marketing)/tools/*` (whois, dns-lookup, port-checker, ssl-checker, etc.) with a `/tools` hub. Read one (e.g. `tools/port-checker`) to match the exact layout/metadata/style. Add THREE new tools, each keyword-optimized (title/H1/meta), on-brand, linked from the `/tools` hub + footer + added to `app/sitemap.ts`, and each with a soft CTA to the relevant Nxeon product:
1. **`/tools/minecraft-server-status`** — "Minecraft Server Status Checker". Input `host` (and optional port, default 25565). A server-side API route (`app/api/tools/mc-status/route.ts`) performs the **Minecraft Server List Ping** (TCP: handshake packet + status request, parse the JSON status) and returns online/offline, players online/max, MOTD, version, and latency. Handle timeouts/offline gracefully. Client shows a nice result card. (This ranks for "minecraft server status" and shows off your MC hosting — link to /minecraft-server-hosting.)
2. **`/tools/server-size-calculator`** — "What VPS / game server do I need?". Client-side: pick a use case (Minecraft/Rust/Palworld/Valheim/website/WordPress/Node app/Discord bot/etc.) + a scale input (players or traffic) → recommend RAM/CPU/storage and **map it to a specific Nxeon plan** with a link to buy/that game page. Use the real specs from `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/keywords-games.md` for the game recommendations. Pull real plan tiers/prices from the DB (don't invent).
3. **`/tools/latency-test`** — "Ping / Latency Test". Client-side: measures round-trip latency from the visitor's browser to a Nxeon endpoint (repeat fetch to a tiny `app/api/tools/ping/route.ts` that returns 200 fast, average the ms), shows the result + "you'll get low latency to Nxeon" + CTA. (If multi-region isn't available, just test the main endpoint and say so honestly.)

## PART 2 — Real-review engine (retire the demo badges with REAL social proof)
- **Prisma model `Review`** (additive): `{ id, author, role, rating Int, body, source (INTERNAL|GOOGLE|TRUSTPILOT|HOSTADVICE), approved Boolean, featured Boolean, createdAt }`. `npx prisma db push`.
- **Admin page** `/admin/reviews` (admin-host-gated, like other admin pages) + actions: add/edit/approve/feature/delete reviews. Also a settings field for the external review-profile URLs (Trustpilot/HostAdvice/Google) — reuse the settings mechanism.
- **Post-purchase review request**: after a successful VPS/hosting purchase (find where an order completes / a server goes ACTIVE), queue an email (reuse the mailer + email templates) that thanks the customer and asks for an honest review, linking the configured external profiles. Send it once per order (guard against duplicates); respect notification prefs. If profile URLs aren't set, skip gracefully.
- **Display**: a "What our customers say" section component fed by APPROVED reviews (featured first). Wire the homepage `components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx` to REAL aggregate data: if ≥1 approved review with a real external score exists, show real counts/scores; else fall back to the current DEMO placeholder (keep the existing `// DEMO PLACEHOLDER` behavior as the fallback so nothing looks empty). Don't fabricate — real data or the clearly-marked demo fallback.

## PART 3 — Launch coupon
Using the existing coupon system (there's a Coupon model + admin coupon CRUD + order-discount logic), create a **launch coupon**: code `LAUNCH50`, 50% off the first term/month, VPS + shared-hosting scoped, with the built per-IP + usage guards (a sane max redemptions, e.g. 500, and 1 per user/IP), active now. Create it via a small seed/script using the existing coupon creation path (so eligibility logic applies), OR if that's unsafe, add it to seed.ts + note the admin can create it. Confirm it validates in the checkout discount flow.

## Finish
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean + `npm run build` pass. Commit (hook pushes GitHub). `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify HTTP 200 + spot-check: `/tools/minecraft-server-status`, `/tools/server-size-calculator`, `/admin/reviews` (307→login is fine), and the coupon exists. Do NOT run promote-production — hand it back.
- Board: comment on the Nxeon board "Marketing Ideas" or "SEO" card noting these shipped.

Report: the 3 tools + their APIs, the review model/admin/email/display + how badges fall back, the launch coupon code + terms, staging verification, the prod deploy note (`bash scripts/promote-production.sh`), and any config needed (external review-profile URLs).

=== prefs.ts ===
/**
 * Notification preferences: the stored shape, the pure helpers — and the POLICY
 * that decides which messages those preferences are allowed to suppress.
 *
 * Plain module (safe to import from server components; client components must
 * import TYPES ONLY — the `mayDeliverTo` helper below reaches for `./db`). The
 * `"use server"` action file may only export async functions, so all of this
 * lives here.
 *
 * WHY THIS FILE GREW A POLICY (2026-07-26)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * `User.notificationPrefs` was written by the settings form and read by NOTHING
 * (QA-PRELAUNCH P1-32). A customer who unticked "Account email" still received
 * every receipt; the "Security alerts" toggle governed a channel that was never
 * built. That is the same defect this codebase keeps shipping: a control that
 * reports success and is read by nothing — the auto-suspend kill switch an
 * operator turned off before watching customer VMs get suspended anyway
 * (P1-5), and the domain-markup panel that displayed 0% while charging 25%
 * (P1-9).
 *
 * The dangerous half of fixing it is OVER-fixing it. If a preference could
 * suppress a declined payment, an imminent suspension, a security/2FA change or
 * a data-loss warning, then an unticked checkbox would silently swallow the one
 * message the customer had to see — and they would lose a server, or an
 * account, with no warning at all. That is strictly worse than the original bug.
 *
 * So suppressibility is decided by a message's TIER, declared once in the
 * catalogue below, and never by the call site. A send site cannot make itself
 * suppressible by passing the wrong flag, and an unrecognised kind resolves to
 * CRITICAL — if we guess wrong, we guess towards "delivered".
 */

export type NotificationPrefs = {
  /**
   * Non-urgent transactional EMAIL: payment receipts, activity notices.
   * Never covers the dunning sequence, suspensions or security changes.
   */
  email: boolean;
  /**
   * Product news / marketing. Unticking this also removes the address from the
   * campaign list (see `updateNotificationPrefs`) — the stored flag alone would
   * suppress nothing, because campaigns are addressed by email, not by user.
   */
  product: boolean;
  /**
   * Legacy key, pinned `true`.
   *
   * It used to render as a "Security alerts" toggle, which was dishonest twice
   * over: the channel it claimed to govern was never built (sign-in / token /
   * 2FA paths write audit rows only), and security, password and 2FA messages
   * must not be suppressible in the first place. Kept in the shape so
   * previously-stored values and the GDPR export keep round-tripping, and typed
   * as the literal `true` so no code path can ever write it back as
   * consent-withdrawn.
   */
  security: true;
};

export const DEFAULT_PREFS: NotificationPrefs = { email: true, product: true, security: true };

/**
 * Normalise whatever is stored in the Json column into a typed prefs object.
 * A missing or malformed key falls back to the default (opted IN) — the column
 * is nullable and predates this policy, so "absent" must never read as "the
 * customer opted out of everything".
 */
export function normalizePrefs(raw: unknown): NotificationPrefs {
  const p = (raw ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
  return {
    email: typeof p.email === "boolean" ? p.email : DEFAULT_PREFS.email,
    product: typeof p.product === "boolean" ? p.product : DEFAULT_PREFS.product,
    security: true,
  };
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*                          Delivery policy                                   */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/** How a message reaches the customer. */
export type NotifyChannel = "email" | "inapp";

/**
 * Suppressibility tier.
 *
 * CRITICAL — "you need to know this". Delivered on every channel, always,
 *            whatever the preferences say. Money that failed to move, a service
 *            about to be suspended or deleted, a change to how the account is
 *            secured, or anything that can cost the customer data.
 * ACCOUNT  — informational transactional. Email is suppressible via
 *            `prefs.email`; the in-app bell is kept (see `isSuppressible`).
 * PRODUCT  — marketing. Suppressible on every channel via `prefs.product`.
 */
export type NotifyTier = "CRITICAL" | "ACCOUNT" | "PRODUCT";

/**
 * Every message kind the platform can send, and the ONE thing that decides
 * whether a preference may hold it back. Grouped by tier so the split is
 * reviewable at a glance — adding a kind is a deliberate act, and putting
 * something in ACCOUNT is a statement that a customer missing it entirely costs
 * them nothing they cannot recover.
 */
export const NOTIFY_KINDS = {
  // ---- CRITICAL: never suppressible, on any channel, by any preference. -----
  /** Password-reset link. The only way back into a locked-out account. */
  password_reset: "CRITICAL",
  /**
   * Email-verification link. CRITICAL for the same reason as the reset link, not

  email_verify: "CRITICAL",

  security_change: "CRITICAL",
  /** Card declined, dunning retry declined, final notice. Money did not move. */
  payment_failed: "CRITICAL",
  /** 3-D Secure / `requires_action` — the payment stalls until the customer acts. */
  payment_action_required: "CRITICAL",

/**
 * Seed / refresh the LAUNCH50 launch coupon.
 *
 * Idempotent: upserts by code, so re-running is safe. Uses the SAME Coupon shape
 * the admin create path (`adminCreateCoupon`) writes, so all of the checkout
 * eligibility logic in lib/coupon-order.ts + the atomic per-user / per-IP claim
 * guards in lib/order.ts apply unchanged.
 *
 * Terms:
 *   code            LAUNCH50
 *   kind/value      PERCENT 50  → 50% off
 *   scope           ORDER       → redeemed at service checkout (not wallet top-up)
 *   serviceKind     VPS         → the product family the checkout coupon flow
 *                                 evaluates (orderQuote scopes orders as VPS).
 *                                 NB: shared-hosting checkout does not yet consume
 *                                 coupons, so VPS is the honest working scope.
 *   maxTermMonths   1           → discount only the first term/month, so a 12-month
 *                                 order can't stretch 50% across a whole year
 *   maxRedemptions  500         → sane global cap
 *   1 per user/IP               → enforced automatically by the unique
 *                                 (coupon,user) + (coupon,ipHash) redemption rows
 *   active          true
 *
 * Run:  npx tsx scripts/seed-launch-coupon.ts
 */
import { db } from "../lib/db";

async function main() {
  const code = "LAUNCH50";
  const data = {
    kind: "PERCENT" as const,
    value: 50,
    scope: "ORDER" as const,
    serviceKind: "VPS" as const,
    planSlug: null,
    maxTermMonths: 1,
    firstTimeOnly: false,
    minAmountCents: null,
    maxRedemptions: 500,
    expiresAt: null,
    active: true,
    note: "Launch promo — 50% off the first term on any VPS. Max 500 redemptions, 1 per user/IP.",
  };

  const coupon = await db.coupon.upsert({
    where: { code },
    update: data,
    create: { code, ...data },
  });

  console.log(`✔ LAUNCH50 ready: ${coupon.value}% off (${coupon.scope}/${coupon.serviceKind}), ` +
    `first ${coupon.maxTermMonths} month, max ${coupon.maxRedemptions}, active=${coupon.active}, ` +
    `redeemed ${coupon.timesRedeemed}.`);
}

main()
  .then(() => process.exit(0))
  .catch((e) => {
    console.error("Failed to seed LAUNCH50:", e);
    process.exit(1);
  });
